known_errors.description: A larger-sample (690-application) re-measurement of the false-positive rate Phase 15 first reported on only 12 GENUINE applications found real, more concerning results: hard-negative accuracy only 55.56% (75/135), the new adversarial pattern 21 (a third legitimate repeat application from the same borrower) misclassified 0/45 (100% wrong, worse than pattern 17's already-poor ~50%), and normal_genuine_baseline (the single simplest, least ambiguous GENUINE case in the whole catalog) only 33.3% accurate (5/15). A real, evidenced-but-not-proven platform-bias correlation was found alongside this: all 10 of normal_genuine_baseline's misclassifications landed on platform B (4/4) or C (6/6), while every platform A (2/2) and D (3/3) instance was correctly cleared - notable because that pattern's own platform assignment is genuinely randomized in the generator (rng.choice(PLATFORMS)), ruling out a generator artifact as the explanation.
known_errors.impact: The trained GNN checkpoint's unreliability is not confined to intentionally adversarial hard negatives - it materially affects the simplest possible genuine case too, and its behavior appears to depend on which platform an application is submitted through, which should not be a legitimate fraud signal on its own.
known_errors.workaround: None implemented - explicitly out of scope for Phase 21 (a measurement/evaluation phase, not model retraining). Hypothesis (not confirmed by an ablation): patterns 17/21 in datasets/scenario_generator.py hardcode their platform (PLATFORMS[1]/'b' and PLATFORMS[2]/'c' respectively, confirmed by grep, never randomized) - combined with Phase 13's already-documented severe overfitting (finalTrainLoss 3.86e-5), this may have taught the model a spurious platform-based shortcut. Retraining with platform assignment randomized and/or a larger, more platform-diverse training set is the natural next step to actually test this hypothesis - flagged for a future ML-focused phase, alongside Phase 20's separate GNN live-inference-collapse finding, which this is believed to be a related symptom of (see ML_MODEL.md's Phase 21 section for the full synthesis).

architecture_decisions.central_db: PostgreSQL only (central-db); graph persisted as relational node/edge tables (graph_nodes/graph_edges, MERGE-style upserts), materialized lazily into an in-memory NetworkX MultiDiGraph on first real graph operation (not eager-at-startup, to preserve the /health-never-depends-on-Postgres guarantee established in Phase 2/8) for GNN/entity-neighborhood queries
architecture_decisions.loan_platform_backend: Node.js + Express, serves built React frontend statically from same container
architecture_decisions.event_delivery: Outbox pattern + polling delivery worker with retry backoff over HTTP(S), no message broker container
architecture_decisions.tokenization: HMAC-SHA256 with HKDF-derived per-purpose keys from one master secret
architecture_decisions.gnn: Hand-rolled lightweight heterogeneous GraphSAGE-style model in plain PyTorch (CPU); no PyG/DGL native extensions - implemented and trained as of Phase 13 (central-fraud-intelligence/src/gnn/, training/); real eval results (97.67% accuracy / 98.63% F1) and a real non-graph-baseline comparison in ML_MODEL.md; wired into the live request path as of Phase 14 (src/gnn/inference.py's GNNScorer, loaded once at FastAPI startup, best-effort) - POST /api/v1/applications/process now returns a real fraudScore and advances status to ANALYZED - combined with a deterministic rule engine's score as of Phase 15 (src/fraud_detection/scoring.py's combine_signals(), 0.6*gnn_score + 0.4*rule_score weighted average) to finally produce real CLEARED/FRAUD_DETECTED status values; real end-to-end evaluation against the full committed dataset measured 73.64%/71.32% accuracy (interleaved/isolated modes) - see ML_MODEL.md's Phase 15 section for the honest gap analysis versus the 97.67% offline GNN-only number
architecture_decisions.docker_networking: Per-platform private net-<id>-db (platform+its own Mongo only), shared net-central-bus (platforms+central app, for events/notifications), private net-central-db (central app+its own Postgres only) - structurally enforces DB isolation requirements ahead of the Phase 29 automated test
architecture_decisions.fraud_detection: Deterministic rule engine (src/fraud_detection/rules.py's evaluate_rules()) implemented and wired into the live request path as of Phase 15 - shared phone/email/name/address tokens to distinct other identities plus shared document-hash reuse, each weighted and scaled by a time-proximity multiplier (application velocity folded into every shared-token signal rather than built as a separate rule, since several SUSPICIOUS/GENUINE hard-negative pairs in the committed dataset share identical graph topology and differ only in timing). Device/bank-token signals remain unimplemented - no platform collects that data yet, the same documented gap since Phase 6. Combined with the GNN score via src/fraud_detection/scoring.py's combine_signals() - see the 'gnn' decision above. - as of Phase 16, every decision this module produces is also explained (src/explainability/explain.py's generate_explanation()): a human-readable summary naming each triggered_rules signal in plain language, and a technical breakdown of each component's real weighted contribution - computed fresh at read time from data this module already stores, never a new pipeline stage or persisted column of its own.
architecture_decisions.explainability: src/explainability/explain.py's generate_explanation() implemented as of Phase 16 - a pure, stateless, read-time function over Phase 15's already-persisted status/fraudScore/ruleScore/triggeredRules/finalRiskScore fields, never touching Postgres, the graph, or the GNN checkpoint, and never persisted as a new column (three documented reasons: nothing to retry against, historical events benefit immediately from later improvements, no redundant derived state stored). Wired into both POST /api/v1/applications/process and GET /api/v1/applications/:id. Deliberately addresses both of Phase 15's open findings within an explicit 'explain honestly, not fix' scope: a CLEARED decision's caveats name the first-arrival blind spot; a GNN-only FRAUD_DETECTED decision's caveats name the legitimate-repeat-applicant limitation and recommend manual review. Neither finding was remediated in this phase.
architecture_decisions.incidents: Only status == FRAUD_DETECTED creates an incident (no CLEARED-near-miss exception - no principled secondary threshold this project's own evaluation data would justify; a borderline CLEARED decision is already surfaced honestly by Phase 16's explanation). An incident's affectedApplications/affectedPlatforms are derived from the same bounded subgraph the rule engine/GNN step already scored (GraphStore.get_relevant_subgraph(), Phase 11) - no new traversal, same horizon as the score that triggered it - so an incident is a genuine point-in-time snapshot (proven by a test: a linked second application's incident lists both applications, the first application's own earlier incident lists only itself). A GNN-only zero-rule-signal FRAUD_DETECTED decision (Phase 15 finding 2) still creates a full incident, not a suppressed one - silently declining to record it would hide a known limitation rather than surface it; the incident carries forward Phase 16's primaryDriver/manual-review-caveat via an explanation snapshot taken at creation time. Idempotency mirrors event ingestion: incident_id is deterministic (INC-<triggering eventId>), triggering_event_id carries a real Postgres UNIQUE constraint with the same ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING * pattern src/ingestion/repository.py uses. review_status defaults OPEN; no transition endpoint built this phase - explicitly left as a Phase 19 dashboard candidate, not an oversight.
architecture_decisions.notifications: One notification row per (incident, affected platform) pair, not one row per incident with an embedded platform list - delivery status is genuinely per-recipient, the same reasoning OutboxEvent already applies one level down at the event level. Notification creation is synchronous inside POST /api/v1/applications/process (gated on incident_row is not None, best-effort/idempotent); delivery is deliberately NOT - a background asyncio poller (NotificationDeliveryWorker) reuses Phase 7's proven outbox pattern (capped exponential backoff, X-Idempotency-Key) running in the opposite direction, so a slow/unreachable platform can never add latency to or fail an otherwise-successful ingestion request. Authentication reuses each platform's own existing shared secret bidirectionally (CENTRAL_ACCEPTS_API_KEY_{A,B,C,D} / each platform's CENTRAL_FRAUD_API_KEY) rather than provisioning a second key-management surface. On the receiving side, alertId is taken directly from the X-Idempotency-Key header (central's own notification_id) since the payload carries no notification id of its own. Deliberately did NOT build POST /api/v1/fraud-notifications (redundant - creation is automatic) or POST /api/v1/fraud-notifications/:id/review (naturally pairs with the incident review workflow already deferred to Phase 19) - the same explicit scope-boundary discipline Phase 17 used for incidents. No reviewed/acknowledged field added to a loan platform's own FraudAlert model either - no review lifecycle was named for platform-side alerts, so adding one now would be premature scaffolding.
architecture_decisions.dashboard: Phase 19: the central app's first-ever UI is a server-rendered Jinja2 app (src/web/), not a React/Vite SPA. Three reasons: (1) requirements.txt had already flagged this exact fork as the open Phase 19 question before this phase began; (2) this service has been 100% Python/FastAPI through Phase 18 - its Dockerfile has no Node build stage at all; (3) a Jinja2 page is testable directly with FastAPI's own TestClient (real HTML in, real HTML out), the same 'test everything for real' discipline every other phase here has kept, which a browser-JS test runner would break. Auth is cookie-based (central_admin_token, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax) but not a second login system - it carries the identical JWT POST /api/v1/admin/login already issues. Zero client-side JavaScript - every mutating action is a plain HTML <form> POST. The graph page renders get_relevant_subgraph()'s own output as node/edge tables, deliberately not a canvas/SVG visualization - a stated scope limit.
architecture_decisions.review_workflow: Phase 19: incident review (POST /api/v1/incidents/:id/review) is a real multi-state transition (OPEN -> UNDER_REVIEW -> CONFIRMED/DISMISSED/ESCALATED, terminal states 409 on further transition), with an append-only {action,by,note,at} review_history JSONB column mirroring loan-platform-a's own ReviewEventSchema field-for-field. Notification/alert acknowledgement (POST /api/v1/fraud-notifications/:id/review centrally, POST /api/v1/admin/fraud-alerts/:alertId/review on each platform) is deliberately simpler - a one-way not-acknowledged -> acknowledged boolean, not a state machine, because a notification doesn't have a lifecycle an admin steers, only one fact worth recording. This is a stated design difference, not an inconsistency between the two review surfaces.
architecture_decisions.metrics: Phase 19: GET /api/v1/metrics is operational counts only (event/incident/notification counts by status, graph node/edge counts) - explicitly NOT performance/latency data, which stays Phase 23's concern. Resolves the ambiguity API.md's Planned table had left open ('19/23') since Phase 0. Every count is a real, live GROUP BY/COUNT query against the real repositories - no caching or pre-aggregation, appropriate at this project's data scale (the same reasoning src/graph/graph_store.py already gives for never needing pruning).

phase20_gating_fix.decision: When no GNN checkpoint is loaded, the ingestion pipeline now advances straight to ANALYZED (fraud_score left None) so the rule engine runs, instead of leaving the event stuck at GRAPH_UPDATED forever.
phase20_gating_fix.rationale: combine_signals() has always documented rule-only decisioning as the correct behavior when gnn_score is None; the live pipeline's gating never actually reached that branch. phase31_two_party_cap.decision: rules.py's evaluate_rules() now caps the combined contribution of token-edge signals (phone/email/name/address) at TWO_PARTY_TOKEN_SCORE_CAP=0.35 when every one of them traces back to the same single other borrower, instead of summing them without limit.
phase31_two_party_cap.rationale: A real user report: two applications that are genuinely the same person applying to two lenders will typically match on several fields at once - that's one piece of evidence (same person), not several independent ones, and summing it without limit made a coincidental, non-fraudulent overlap look like strong fraud evidence. Does not apply when signals point to different other borrowers (a real multi-party/hub pattern), and doesn't touch the document-hash or hub-bonus signals. Measured to have zero effect on the old, saturated GNN checkpoint's final decisions (see phase31_gnn_retrain) - only became reachable in practice once the checkpoint was retrained.

phase31_gnn_retrain.decision: Fixed a hardcoded-platform training bias in two scenario-generator patterns, regenerated the training dataset at --instances-per-pattern 6 (129->258 applications), added an L2 --weight-decay flag to training/train.py, and retrained with --weight-decay 1e-4 --dropout 0.2 (dropout was 0.1).
phase31_gnn_retrain.rationale: Phase 21 evidenced but did not confirm that patterns 17/21 hardcoding their platform assignment (PLATFORMS[1]/PLATFORMS[2]) taught the model a spurious platform-based shortcut, contributing to severe overfitting (finalTrainLoss 3.86e-05 on only 86 training applications) and poor false-positive resistance (55.6% hard-negative accuracy on a 690-application stress test, with legitimate_repeated_application_three_times at 0/45 correct). After this phase's fix + retrain, hard-negative accuracy on that same 690-application dataset is 100% and legitimate_repeated_application_three_times is 45/45 - the strongest available evidence the hypothesis was correct. Training loss still fell to 0.0004 despite the added regularization; recall on genuinely fraudulent two-party overlaps dropped slightly (72.2%->69.4%), traced to a pre-existing early-arrival scoring limitation rather than a new regression - reported honestly in ML_MODEL.md's Phase 31 section rather than smoothed over.
